title: Popol Vuh in K'iche' — the Ximénez Manuscript (Newberry Library, Ayer MS 1515, World Digital Library) and Brasseur de Bourbourg's First Edition of the K'iche' Text (1861)

license.payload: Public domain: the K'iche' text was set down in the Latin alphabet in the sixteenth century; Francisco Ximénez's transcription and Spanish translation (c. 1701–03) survives in the Newberry Library, Ayer MS 1515. The manuscript as digitized for the World Digital Library: Library of Congress, World Digital Library collection (the Library states it is unaware of any copyright or other restrictions; credit line: [Original Source citation], World Digital Library). Brasseur de Bourbourg's Popol Vuh (Paris: Durand, 1861), the first edition of the K'iche' text, is public domain; Internet Archive scan.

normalization: Files as fetched. Internet Archive OCR text layers as fetched, uncorrected (text/<slug>.ocr.txt); the scan under original/ is the witness. Library of Congress and FAMSI PDFs are image files without a text layer: the page is the only reading.
scope: The Popol Vuh in its one surviving witness, Ximénez's manuscript, and in the first printed edition of its K'iche' text. Ximénez's Spanish alone (Scherzer, Vienna, 1857) is a translation and is not seated. Modern editions (Christenson, Colop, Tedlock, Recinos) are in copyright and are not seated.

why_seated: The K'iche' book of the council: the creation, the failed peoples of mud and wood, the Hero Twins in Xibalba, and the lineages of the K'iche' lords. A book whose preamble says it is written again because the original can no longer be seen: the archive's line on books that survive as their own transmission meets it there.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-23: "detour for an ea-corpora searing. lets see. whats available of mayan texts? and then i dont think we have much or any deteurocanonical second temple lit - all those apocalypses. and what about the ethiopian canon? and euclid. all in original language or as close to it as possible. what else?" — "and the Egyptian book of the dead" — "and what about the fragments of the book of baalim? i might be miswriting this. recent discovery. if theyre available anywhere." — "yes yes yes to all - what a meal."
